title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
prompt:
A sorted array of distinct values was rotated at an unknown pivot. Return the index of `target`, or `-1`, in O(log n).

**Example**: `nums = [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]`, `target = 0` → `4`.

At each step one half `[lo..mid]` or `[mid..hi]` is properly sorted — figure out which, then decide whether `target` lies inside it.
hints: If `nums[lo] <= nums[mid]`, the LEFT half is sorted; otherwise the RIGHT half is.
In the sorted half, a simple range check tells you if target is there — go there, else go the other way.
Standard `while (lo <= hi)` with `mid` recomputed each iteration.

solution.explanation: A rotated array always has one sorted half around the midpoint. Identifying it lets you use an ordinary range test to keep or discard that half, preserving O(log n). The `<=` in `nums[lo] <= nums[mid]` correctly handles the two-element case where lo == mid.
